text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Algerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for them.
- Long night of conspiracy ahead of submission today (Sunday) of government programme before parliament.
- Great polemic over privatisation of farming land. But the idea is not new and has already been adopted, last December, by the council of ministers.

- SOS over water situation for the capital, Algiers. With the current 18 million cub metres capacity of the Keddara dam which supplies the city, and authorised consumption of 4.5 million cubic metres per month, Algerians have only three more months water suppies. "After that, the future is uncertain unless weather conditions improve."
- Victims of "terrorism" are living a calvary in the absence of anyone really tackling their problems. Because of lack of medical followup they become prisoners of traumatism.
- Distribution of water may be privatised.
